div.div: Beats add up to a dwell time, dwell plus reset is the cycle, and the cycle sets visitors per hour: 80 s [I1] + 20 s [I2] = 100 s [I3] -> 36 per hour [I4] in theory, about 25 [I5] in a real queue (illustrative budget)
A. ONE VISIT AS TIMED BEATS, to scale (5.6 px per second). Each bar starts where the previous beat ends.
greet: look up, wave, one short line: 6 s [I6]
reply window: listening armed after the line ends: 12 s [I7]
converse: a few turns (largest, most variable): 35 s [I8]
offer: self-serve gift, includes the take timer: 15 s [I9]
inside the offer: no-take timer 12 s [I12]
inside converse: one visitor turn is capped at 10 s [I13]
typical interaction = sum of the six beats: 80 s [I1] [calc]
global inactivity timeout (any beat -> goodbye): 45 s [I14]
'chatty visitor' cap and session-lease maximum: 150 s [I15]

Timeouts are failsafes set ABOVE the intended length, not targets.
The greet line is short on purpose: the reply window opens only when it ends, so a longer greeting delays the visitor's natural reply.
B. THE ARITHMETIC RUNS BOTH WAYS: the cycle sets the queue, and the queue sets how long any beat may be.

x queue friction 0.7 [I16]
= about 25 per hour [I5] [calc]

x show day 6 h [I17]
= about 150 visits per day [I18] [calc]
feeds other gates: endurance gate 150 cycles without intervention [I19]; gift tray and refill cadence must keep up

Throughput is 3600 divided by the CYCLE, not by the dwell: the reset counts. Need more visitors per hour? Cap the converse beat (largest, most variable) or shorten the reset; every second removed from the reset returns to visitors. Report the dwell distribution (median and a high percentile), not only the mean: the cap exists for the tail.
C. THE RESPONSIVENESS BUDGET: from the visitor's consent action to a VISIBLE listening signal, every stage named (to scale, ms).
budget 500 ms [I20] = detection 300 ms [I21] + permit, audio gate, indicator 200 ms [I22]
The robot need not match humans, but each stage is measured on the real robot and network.

Legend: solid bars = planned beat lengths | dashed bars = timers and caps (failsafes) | dashed vertical lines = totals (A) or public reference limits (C). All robot durations are illustrative design values, not measurements.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (a paper, standard or physics value, or my arithmetic on one); [In] = illustrative (a round design value of the right order; never a measurement of a real robot or visitor); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/A2-beats-and-dwell-budget.md (budget table, from beats to throughput, short beats that start early, the responsiveness budget, 'throughput is 3600 divided by the cycle'); C2 for the endurance gate. [calc]: 80 = sum of six beats; 80 + 20 = 100 s; 3600 / 100 = 36 per hour; 36 x 0.7 = 25 (rounded); 25 x 6 h = 150 visits; 300 + 200 = 500 ms.
[I1] interaction_typical_illustrative = 80 s. illustrative: my arithmetic: sum of the six beat_*_illustrative values
[I2] reset_turnover_illustrative = 20 s. illustrative time to reset and let the next visitor step up
[I3] cycle_illustrative = 100 s. illustrative: my arithmetic: interaction_typical_illustrative + reset_turnover_illustrative
[I4] throughput_theoretical_illustrative = 36 visitors per hour. illustrative: my arithmetic: 3600 s / cycle_illustrative
[I5] throughput_realistic_illustrative = 25 visitors per hour. illustrative: my arithmetic: throughput_theoretical_illustrative x queue_friction_factor_illustrative, rounded
[I6] beat_greet_illustrative = 6 s. illustrative beat length
[I7] beat_reply_window_illustrative = 12 s. illustrative listening-armed window after the greeting
[I8] beat_converse_illustrative = 35 s. illustrative conversation beat (a few turns)
[I9] beat_offer_illustrative = 15 s. illustrative self-serve gift offer including the take timer
[I10] beat_celebrate_illustrative = 8 s. illustrative
[I11] beat_goodbye_illustrative = 4 s. illustrative
[I12] take_timer_illustrative = 12 s. illustrative no-take timeout inside beat_offer_illustrative
[I13] per_turn_cap_illustrative = 10 s. illustrative cap on one visitor turn
[I14] inactivity_timeout_illustrative = 45 s. illustrative global inactivity timeout
[I15] interaction_cap_illustrative = 150 s. illustrative 'chatty visitor' cap and session-lease maximum
[I16] queue_friction_factor_illustrative = 0.7 dimensionless. illustrative discount for crowd and queue friction
[I17] show_day_illustrative = 6 h. illustrative show day
[I18] visits_per_day_illustrative = 150 visits. illustrative: my arithmetic: throughput_realistic_illustrative x show_day_illustrative
[I19] consecutive_cycles_gate_illustrative = 150 visitor cycles without intervention. illustrative launch gate
[I20] listening_indicator_budget_illustrative = 500 ms from consent action to visible listening signal. illustrative design budget; chosen below response_limit_flow
[I21] listening_indicator_detect_illustrative = 300 ms (detection share of the budget). illustrative split of listening_indicator_budget_illustrative
[I22] listening_indicator_signal_illustrative = 200 ms (permit + gate + indicator share). illustrative split; sums with listening_indicator_detect_illustrative to the budget
[P23] response_limit_instant = 0.1 s. public: Nielsen 1993, ch. 5
[P24] turn_gap_typical = 200 ms. public: Stivers et al., 'Universals and cultural variation in turn-taking in conversation', PNAS 106(26), 2009: offsets between turns cluster around a short gap of about 200 ms across 10 languages
[P25] response_limit_flow = 1 s. public: Nielsen, Usability Engineering, 1993, ch. 5: about 1 s is the limit for the user's flow of thought to stay uninterrupted; 0.1 s feels instantaneous; 10 s loses attention
